findings_and_qualified_questions.first_failed_contract: A phase-height gate should evaluate every complete post-calibration review cycle that its stated policy requires, but phase-height inputs for terrain-classified scenarios are filtered through the first-wrap warmup twice.
findings_and_qualified_questions.reasoning: FlatGridWalk20 and FlatGridRun55 carry FlatGrid, classify as Terrain and request a three-cycle selected plan. scenario_metrics removes the first observed wrap for all terrain metrics, then passes that already-filtered slice to phase range, contact-to-passing gain and visual peaks, each of which removes through the next wrap again. If at least two wraps occur in captured phase, the first post-calibration interval is absent from those three measurements. This contradicts the adjacent peak-loop comment that every complete post-warmup cycle is independently gated. The old P17 source has the same nested warmup calls for terrain-classified data.
findings_and_qualified_questions.qualification: A full plan does not prove particular runtime phase wraps or values. The finding is conditional on an observed second wrap and a complete affected cycle; no viewer, scenario, fixture or whole-report acceptance was run. Other continuity and independent gates still inspect their own inputs. Exact intended calibration versus review-cycle policy requires an owner decision.
findings_and_qualified_questions.future_repair_direction: Choose and retain a single explicit calibration boundary for applicable height measurements and their review-cycle coverage; ensure any required complete post-calibration cycle contributes without inventing data or altering legitimate trailing partial-cycle exclusions.

findings_and_qualified_questions.first_failed_contract: Finite captured quaternion components alone do not witness a valid normalization or finite derived angular measurement, yet a NaN derived rotation does not update the scalar maximum.
findings_and_qualified_questions.qualification: The final finite-bone predicate tests component finiteness, not nonzero quaternion norm or frame body rotation. Current metrics normalizes captured bone quaternions and later tests `rotation > maximum`; if that operation yields NaN, the comparison cannot increase the max, including ragdoll’s local rotation gate. The actual native normalization behavior, zero/nonunit input reachability, and other independently effective gates have not been proved. Historical P17 passed computed rotation through AngularMagnitudeDegrees::from_degrees, whose checked_nonnegative rejects nonfinite values.

nonfindings: Current whole-report completion requires exact selected plan and every REPORT_BONES key, including pelvis, with separately required finite bone components; missing bone alone is not proof of successful report.
A missing expected phase-height scenario is an explicit optional mode; old and current displayed choices select the same four named scenarios. Do not turn every None into failure.

For applicable phase-height scenarios, no complete measured cycle makes visual_height_peaks return (0,false), and zero fallback range/gain fails the positive 0.025m minimum. Thus those particular empty inputs are not a demonstrated successful height gate.
Both historical and current logic deliberately excludes initial setup pair and trailing partial cycles; future coverage changes must preserve policy rather than treating all exclusions as defective.
Exact full other support bodies, prior root reader scopes, product behavior and unseen derived quaternion semantics are not claimed.
